saints.name: Sergius of Radonezh
saints.sourceTitle: Repose of Venerable Sergius the Wonderworker, Abbot of Radonezh

summary.text: Sergius is remembered as a monastic founder and abbot of Radonezh. The OCA account relates his family, early formation, community, and repose in 1392. It includes miracles and traditions about his influence on the Church and society. Those episodes remain part of the identified hagiographic narrative, while related historical lessons provide additional context for medieval Rus.

blocks.text: Baptized Bartholomew, Sergius grew up near Rostov and Radonezh. After his parents’ death, he and his widowed brother Stephen built a forest church dedicated to the Trinity.

blocks.text: The settlement became a community. Sergius was ordained, worked alongside the brethren, and developed common monastic life. The published life also recounts his blessing of Dmitry before Kulikovo.

blocks.text: Sister Ioanna’s monastery account emphasizes how reluctant Sergius was to accept ecclesiastical honors. It says that he accepted priestly ordination and leadership of his own monastery only reluctantly and refused the office of Metropolitan of Moscow. The account links the growth of other northern monasteries to the work of his disciples.

blocks.text: The original wooden Trinity church burned and was replaced by a white stone church in 1422. Sister Ioanna’s account connects Andrei Rublev’s iconographic work, including the famous Trinity icon, with that later church. It also relates the discovery of Sergius’s relics during construction and the tradition of their incorruption. These are parts of the monastery’s account of his subsequent veneration.
